title: secp256k1-ecdlp: negation + GLV-endomorphism parallel Pollard rho (v2, corrected)

claims.statement: Revision of rejected submission 16547c5b-f2c2-44b0-a5fc-36e43094af47, fixing all four stated objections: (1) branch points are now R_h=[c_h]P+[d_h]Q (mixed P- and Q-multiples; the prior pure-P-multiple branches left b permanently at 0, making the construction unable to ever solve for x -- experiment.py now reports b_nonzero_step_count directly to confirm the fix); (2) the success-probability threshold is verified in exact 60-digit decimal arithmetic (0.390000...000339... >= 0.39), not a rounded display constant; (3) the construction is now W=1024 independent parallel walks (van Oorschot & Wiener 1999) so the pinned 6M batched-affine reference price is legitimately justified via per-round batch inversion across the W simultaneous additions, rather than an unjustified sequential-walk claim; (4) peak memory now uses a specified distinguished-point hash table (theta=2^-60) rather than an unspecified full-history structure, reducing the claim to ~2^73.699243 bytes. Total computation (including the W/theta=2^70 distinguished-point tail overhead, itemized per-step overhead, setup and verification) is at most 2.370167e+38 reference-group-operation equivalents (pinned C=1,000). The GLV lambda and matching field-side beta were independently re-derived via Tonelli-Shanks and checked against the protected generator with real curve arithmetic.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the production mechanism exactly: W parallel walks, mixed c_h/d_h branch points, orbit-canonicalization, distinguished-point-only storage, fruitless-cycle escape, linear-solve. Reports b_nonzero_step_count and wrong_answers directly so a reviewer can verify both the v1 bug fix and that the construction never returns an incorrect scalar. Does not validate production curve arithmetic, instruction costs or full-size timing.
